terms.def: Abbreviated new drug application, for a generic. Changes follow 314.70 through 314.97; labeling follows the reference listed drug.
The Swiss list of variations, revised from 1 February 2026 and harmonised as far as possible with the EU list.
A change notified within 12 months of implementation, usually in a yearly group.
The yearly report to an approved application. Minor changes are made first and described in it; it is due within 60 days of the anniversary of approval (21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)).
One notification of the Type IA changes made over up to 12 months.
The legally binding entries of the Japanese approval form (Module 1.2).
A notification of labelling or package leaflet changes not connected with the SmPC; not a variation.
Biologics license application. Changes follow 21 CFR 601.12.
Supplement - Changes Being Effected. Product made with the change can be distributed when FDA receives the supplement.
Supplement - Changes Being Effected in 30 Days. Distribution can start 30 days after FDA receives the supplement, unless FDA objects in that time.
Company core data sheet: the company's reference safety and prescribing information that regional labels follow.
FDA's inspection of a site against current good manufacturing practice. Whether a new site has a satisfactory one for the operation drives the category of a site move.
Japan's post-approval change management protocol: confirmed in step 1, then changes are notified in step 2.
The pause in an assessment while the holder answers the authority's questions.
The comparison of a biological product before and after a manufacturing change (ICH Q5E).
FDA's term for a post-approval change management protocol: a plan, approved in advance, that lets a future change be filed in a lower category.
A change made before the agency is told (US annual report, EU Type IA).
A supplement with clinical data, for example a new indication or population.
A legally binding element of the dossier; changing it needs a regulatory submission in the category set by its risk (ICH Q12).
Under ICH Q12, the legally binding elements of the approved application. Changes to other elements are managed in the quality system.
A change to strength, pharmaceutical form or route of administration (and the other changes in Annex I), assessed like a new application.
The last compound synthesized before the reaction that produces the drug substance.
Applications for permission to import (CT-18) or manufacture (CT-21) a new drug.
The transmittal form for periodic reports, including annual reports.
The application form for new applications and supplements.
Draft amendment of 2 February 2026 to the NDCT Rules that would add Level I to III for post-approval quality changes.
Generic Drug User Fee Amendments. GDUFA III sets FDA's review goals for ANDA supplements in fiscal years 2023 to 2027.
Several related variations to one authorisation in one submission; the group follows its highest type (Article 7).
A change implemented and notified at once; accepted unless WHO objects.
A change with substantial potential to affect the product, filed as an SNDS or SANDS; implemented only after a new Notice of Compliance.
PAC/2024 levels: supplement and notifiable change need approval; annual notification is reported in the first quarter; record of change is kept under GMP.
A minor change implemented without prior review and then reported with the Level III form.
A change with substantial potential to have an adverse effect on the product; needs a prior approval supplement.
Needs WHO's letter of acceptance before implementation.
A change with minimal potential for an adverse effect; reported in the annual report.
Notification within 30 days after changing an item marked as a minor change item in the approval form.
Implemented if WHO has not started correspondence within 60 days of acknowledging it.
A change with moderate potential for an adverse effect; reported in a CBE-30 or CBE-0 supplement.
Extended- or delayed-release products. Changes that may affect their release are treated as major in the US.
When related changes are filed together, they take the category of the strictest one (guidance section XII).
Several variations for one product filed together and processed on the longest time limit.
New drug application, including 505(b)(2) applications. Changes follow 21 CFR 314.70.
Health Canada's letter that allows a notifiable change to be implemented.
A Level II quality change for biologics and radiopharmaceuticals, implemented after a No Objection Letter; review target 90 days.
CDSCO's guidance on post-approval changes in biological products (version 1.2, implemented 16 May 2024).
Post-approval change management protocol (ICH Q12). In the US, a comparability protocol.
Approval needed before changing an approved matter in the Japanese approval form.
Prescription Drug User Fee Act. PDUFA VII sets FDA's review goals for NDA and BLA supplements in fiscal years 2023 to 2027.
Product lifecycle management document: a summary of established conditions, their reporting categories, protocols and commitments.
A supplement FDA must approve before product made with the change is distributed.
The approved drug a generic is compared with. ANDA labeling follows it.
Reference member state: the authority that leads mutual recognition and decentralised procedures.
FDA's notice under section 505(o)(4) of the FD&C Act that new safety information should be added to the labeling; the holder responds within 30 days.
CDSCO's online portal for applications, including post-approval changes.
Scale-up and post-approval changes guidances (IR, MR, SS). Their categories still apply to components and composition changes.
The same Type IA or IA-IN change for several authorisations of the same holder in one notification (Article 7a).
Dossier content that is not an established condition; changes are managed in the quality system.
A change notified to the agency before or when it is made, with no wait for approval (US CBE-0 and CBE-30, EU Type IB after 30 days).
A minor variation implemented first and notified within 12 months, for example in the annual update.
A minor variation implemented first and notified immediately afterwards.
A minor variation notified before implementation and accepted if no objection is raised within 30 days. Also the default for unclassified changes.
A major variation that may significantly affect quality, safety or efficacy; it needs approval before implementation.
One assessment by a reference authority of the same change to several authorisations of the same holder (Article 20).
